title: "Search strategy"
---

This page records the search, as PRISMA-S requires [@rethlefsen2021]. The counts are the records each database returned before deduplication. [01-deduplication](../analysis/01-deduplication.ipynb) writes the identification counts for the flow diagram from the exports in `data/raw/search_exports/` once the exports are in.

## Query

One query runs in Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed. It searches titles for a form of *share* within five words of *data*, and leaves out titles that name blockchain, smart contracts, the Internet of Things, vehicular networks, edge computing, or cloud computing. It covers sources published from 2015 to 2025 in English and French and applies no document type filter. Development and testing, below, gives how it was chosen and how well it performs.

| Database | Records |
|:--|--:|
| PubMed | 2,437 |
| Scopus | 7,067 |
| Web of Science | 6,149 |
| **Total** | **15,653** |

: Records the query returned on 18 November 2026 through each database's API, before deduplication. Matched on DOI, or on title and year, they come to 7,933. The Web of Science count omits the language limit, which its API rejects beside a proximity search. {#tbl-records}

Platforms and search dates for the exports are to be added.

## Development and testing

**Method.** Candidate queries were tested against known relevant sources, following the development and validation set approach of @hausner2012. The known sources are the 76 sources included by @chawinga2019 that meet this review's criteria apart from year. A script rebuilt their list from the paper, and a local language model checked each source against the criteria. Sources published 2007 to 2014 form the development set: 45 sources, 35 of them indexed in at least one database. Sources published from 2015 form the test set: 31 sources, 25 indexed, held out until the query was chosen.

Each candidate ran in PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science, with two counts: the records it returns for 2015 to 2025 in English or French, and the development sources it finds by DOI or PMID. A candidate dropped out when another found at least as many development sources in fewer records. Every measurement here can be checked or rerun in the [search development notebook](../analysis/00_search-development/00-search-development.ipynb), which holds each run with its code and files.

**Candidates compared.**

| Query | Records | Development sources found |
|:--|--:|--:|
| "data sharing" plus factor words (barrier, policy, incentive…) | 14,255 | 28 |
| *share* within 3 words of *data*, title | 9,591 | 28 |
| *share* within 5 words of *data*, title | 10,493 | 29 |
| *share* within 5 words of *data*, title, OR "data sharing" plus factor words | 18,135 | 31 |
| ***share* within 5 words of *data*, title, excluding computing words (the query)** | **7,933** | **29** |

: Records across the three databases with duplicates removed, and development sources found, of 35. {#tbl-candidates tbl-colwidths="[64,18,18]"}

Searching abstracts as well returns about eight times the records for at most three more sources. Runs 5 to 15 hold the measurements.

**Results.**

- **Test set:** the query finds 18 of the 25 indexed test sources, a relative recall of 0.72 (95% interval 0.52 to 0.86). That is 8 of 11 in PubMed, 16 of 23 in Scopus and 12 of 18 in Web of Science (run 16).
- **What it misses:** the missed test sources name research data management, open data or open science in their titles.
- **Terms that would catch them:** title terms for these add 489 to 5,351 records each, for one to five test sources (run 21). They stay out of the query, and the 13 test sources it misses are added by hand (see [Other sources](#other-sources)).

**Limits.**

- The development result is in-sample, because the query was chosen to find as many development sources as possible. Only the test result estimates recall.
- The test set is small and dates from 2015 to 2018, so recall for sources from 2019 to 2025 is untested.
- Opening tier 2 to all source types came after the first test result. It raised the test sources in scope from 10 to 25.

**Peer review.** A McGill health sciences librarian reviewed the search approach on 27 October 2026.

## Search strings

### Generic query

```text
Title: share* NEAR/5 data
NOT
Title: blockchain* OR "smart contract*" OR IoT OR "internet of things" OR vehicular OR "edge computing" OR cloud

Limits: published 2015 to 2025; English or French
```

### PubMed

PubMed's proximity search takes no truncation, so the string writes out four forms of *share*.

```text
(
  ("sharing data"[ti:~5] OR "shared data"[ti:~5] OR "share data"[ti:~5] OR "shares data"[ti:~5])
  NOT (blockchain*[ti] OR "smart contract*"[ti] OR IoT[ti] OR "internet of things"[ti]
       OR vehicular[ti] OR "edge computing"[ti] OR cloud[ti])
)
AND 2015:2025[dp]
AND (english[la] OR french[la])
```

### Scopus

Scopus applies AND NOT after every AND, so the limits come first and the NOT clause last.

```text
TITLE ( shar* W/5 data )
AND PUBYEAR > 2014 AND PUBYEAR < 2026
AND LANGUAGE ( english OR french )
AND NOT TITLE ( blockchain* OR "smart contract*" OR IoT OR "internet of things"
                OR vehicular OR "edge computing" OR cloud )
```

### Web of Science

```text
(
  TI=( shar* NEAR/5 data )
  NOT TI=( blockchain* OR "smart contract*" OR IoT OR "internet of things"
           OR vehicular OR "edge computing" OR cloud )
)
AND PY=(2015-2025)
AND LA=(English OR French)
```

## Other sources {#other-sources}

These sources meet the eligibility criteria and are added by hand. The first 13 are test sources the query misses. The last three were identified during search development.

- Chiware and Mathe (2016). Academic libraries' role in research data management services: a South African perspective, doi:10.7553/81-2-1563
- Chigwada et al. (2017). Research data management in research institutions in Zimbabwe, doi:10.5334/dsj-2017-031

Name the export file for these sources with the prefix `other-`, for example `other-hand-added_2026-11-18.ris`.

## Export file names

Name each export `<database>_<YYYY-MM-DD>.<ext>`, for example `scopus_2026-11-18.ris`. The date is the search date. Supported formats are RIS and CSV. See the README in `data/raw/search_exports/`.
